mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate below 5.0% signals an easing monetary policy that reduces discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 5.0%.

mechanism_narrative: When year-over-year CPI inflation exceeds 3.5%, it triggers expectations of aggressive monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL YoY exceeds 3.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in nonfarm payrolls and declines in unemployment rate signal labor market strength that boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS rises and UNRATE falls as per trigger.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion, housing starts below 1300 thousand units signal weakening consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when HOUST < 1300.0 and GDPC1 growth (QoQ) > 1.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A rising industrial production index above 100.0 indicates robust manufacturing activity that supports corporate earnings growth, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO > 100.0.

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment rate falls below 3.5%, it signals labor market tightness that may trigger wage inflation and monetary policy tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE < 3.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in retail sales and housing starts signal strong consumer demand that drives corporate revenue growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when RSAFS and HOUST both rise as per trigger.

mechanism_narrative: In high-inflation regimes, CPIAUCSL above 4.0% signals persistent inflation requiring aggressive rate hikes, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL > 4.0% and CPIAUCSL YoY > 4.0% for 3 consecutive months.
